headline: 97.2 g/t GOLD OVER 6.3m TRUE WIDTH — OceanaGold Wharekirauponga Hits Highest Grades to Date; Processing Expansion to 1.2M tpa Under Review
snippet: OceanaGold (TSX/NYSE: OGC) released results from 16 drill holes at Wharekirauponga, New Zealand on September 24, headlined by WKP146C returning an estimated true width of 6.3 metres at 97.2 g/t Au and WKP150 cutting 8.5 metres at 41.5 g/t Au — among the highest-grade intercepts ever reported at the project, extending the EG Vein zone into areas currently outside of reported reserves. OceanaGold simultaneously reported progress at Waihi North and revealed it is evaluating a processing expansion to 1.2 million tonnes per year (up from 0.8Mt) ahead of a Waihi District technical report due January 2027.

headline: 14.82 g/t AUEG OVER 8m IN SCHIST — Collective Mining Hits New Tungsten-Gold Zone OUTSIDE Apollo Resource at 927m Depth; 13 Rigs Running
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX/Nasdaq: CNL) announced September 24 that drill hole APC150-D4 at the Guayabales Project in Caldas, Colombia cut 8.15 metres at 14.82 g/t AuEq (0.40% WO3, 8.47 g/t Au, 4 g/t Ag) beginning 927 metres below surface — the first tungsten found in schist outside the southern margin of the Apollo breccia body, opening a new drilling target in a unit that extends from surface to over 1,000 metres vertical and is largely untested. With 13 diamond rigs active, 96 holes awaiting assay, and metallurgical recoveries confirmed at 95% Au, 92% Ag, 85% Cu, 70% W, the discovery adds a critical-mineral dimension to what is already one of the more advanced porphyry-breccia systems in Colombia.

headline: NIGER HANDS 40% TO STATE, ATOMIC EAGLE TAKES 60% — Madaouela Convention Formally Executed; GoviEx Arbitration Dropped; Post-France Uranium Era Begins
snippet: Niger's military government and Australia's Atomic Eagle (ASX: AEU) formally executed the Madaouela mining convention on September 23, restructuring ownership of the project near Arlit to Niger 40% (15% free-carry, 25% paying stake) and Atomic Eagle 60% with full operational control — requiring staged payments of US$5 million on an exploitation permit and a further US$5 million at construction start. The deal formalises a framework announced in August and extinguishes the international arbitration proceedings launched by previous licence holder GoviEx, cementing the junta's post-coup pivot away from French and Canadian operators toward partners willing to cede larger state stakes.

headline: $330M DEBT MANDATE FOR CORANI SILVER — Natixis CIB to Lead Fully Underwritten 7-Year Facility for Peru Giant; Highlander Reports $100M Cash, Zero Debt
snippet: Highlander Silver Corp. (TSXV/Nasdaq: HSLV) announced September 23 that Natixis CIB has been mandated to lead a fully underwritten 7-year senior secured $330 million project finance facility for the Corani Silver Project in Peru — one of the world's largest undeveloped silver deposits — plus a $100 million cost overrun facility that Highlander will provide before first draw. With approximately $100 million cash and no debt as of June 30, the company is positioned to bridge to a Q1 2027 facility close; the mandate marks Corani's transition from development-stage asset to a fully-funded construction-track project.

headline: GLENCORE HITS ASX OCT 14 — No New Shares, Just CHESS Units Pitched at Australia's A$4.4T Pension Pool to Bankroll 1.6M Tonne Copper Push
snippet: Glencore confirmed September 24 it will begin trading on the ASX under ticker GLC on October 14 via CHESS Depositary Interests — a secondary listing with no capital raise or new share issuance, designed to tap Australia's A$4.4 trillion superannuation system as a long-term capital source. CEO Gary Nagle said the company aims for ASX 200 inclusion within 12 months and that the listing supports its copper growth strategy targeting approximately 1.6 million metric tonnes annually by 2035, roughly double current output — at a time when the copper market is simultaneously grappling with Escondida's ongoing shutdown and a widening physical split between tariff-inflated US inventories and genuinely tight LME stocks.

headline: 18m AT 0.42% TUNGSTEN — Viking Mines Confirms Multiple Thick RC Intercepts Below Historic Nevada Mine; VKA Surges 25%
snippet: Viking Mines (ASX: VKA) jumped 25% on September 24 after the latest RC drilling below the historic Linka Mine in Nevada confirmed thick tungsten intercepts — including 18 metres at 0.42% WO3 and 13 metres at 0.46% WO3, grades consistent with the mine's 1950s production history. The 20-hole maiden programme has returned an 86% drill-hole success rate; assays from holes around Linka Main are pending around mid-October. Nevada-hosted, US-critical-mineral tungsten is attracting defence and industrial investors as China controls roughly 85% of global refined tungsten supply.

headline: HKEX TO LAUNCH YUAN GOLD FUTURES EARLY 2027 — Hong Kong Bids for Global Gold Hub as Mainland Imports Hit 107 Tonnes in July
snippet: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing announced September 24 it will launch a yuan-denominated gold futures contract early next year, building on a gold clearing and settlement system launched in mid-2026, as part of a direct bid to challenge London and New York's dominance of global gold benchmarks. Officials framed the move as a yuan internationalisation play and a commodities hub strategy at a time when mainland Chinese demand has surged: Hong Kong gold imports hit 107 tonnes in July 2026, up nearly 50% from February's 72 tonnes, reinforcing Asia's growing weight in global bullion flows.

headline: 46 DAYS TO CHINA RARE EARTH DEADLINE — November 10 Pause Expires; US Defense Races to De-Risk from Beijing's Extraterritorial Magnet Licensing
snippet: China's one-year suspension of rare earth export controls runs out on November 10, 2026 — 46 days from today — with no extension announced, putting EV, wind energy, and defence supply chains on notice that Beijing's licensing regime could restrict access to any magnet containing even 0.1% Chinese-origin rare earth content. China's rare-earth magnet exports to the US fell 21% in August to 512 tonnes, suggesting the regime is already influencing flows before the pause expires; the IEA estimates US$6.5 trillion in annual Western downstream production is exposed to the licensing system, in a supply chain where China mines 70%, processes 90%, and manufactures 93% of finished magnets.

headline: US COMEX HOLDS 69% OF GLOBAL COPPER STOCKS — Tariff Front-Running Fills American Warehouses While Europe Tightens and Escondida Stays Dark
snippet: A structural split is emerging in global copper markets: COMEX warehouses now hold approximately 69% of all exchange-tracked copper stocks — driven by tariff front-running that has concentrated roughly 1 million tonnes in US facilities inaccessible to European and Asian industrial buyers — while LME stocks fell 1,625 tonnes in a single session to 254,250 tonnes, signalling genuine physical tightening outside North America. The divergence is compressing LME prices back toward $14,600/MT after the September 22 record of $14,875, while BHP's Escondida — the world's largest copper mine — remains shut after a fatal accident on September 23, with no restart timeline given.

headline: OROSUR ANZA PLACEMENT OVERSUBSCRIBED AT C$14M — Strong Demand for Colombia Gold Drill Play; El Cedro Program Funded into Late 2027
snippet: Orosur Mining's (TSX-V/AIM: OMI) C$14 million brokered private placement to fund drilling at the Anza gold project in Colombia closed oversubscribed and fully allocated as of September 25, with proceeds directed almost exclusively at the El Cedro discovery — an epithermal gold target in Antioquia generating investor interest against the backdrop of Buriticá comparables. Led by Red Cloud Securities with UK brokers Turner Pope and Greenwood Capital, the raise — priced at C$0.32 per unit with a 24-month warrant at C$0.32 — gives Orosur a funded drilling runway into late 2027 as it pursues a maiden resource at Anza.
